items.title: Kenya confirms a ninth Ebola case, with 134 of 135 contacts in quarantine
items.summary: The Washington Post and Al Jazeera report that Kenya's health ministry confirmed a ninth Ebola case on 20 October, a contact of the first patient who tested positive while already in quarantine. The ministry says there is still no evidence of spread beyond known contacts. Officials have identified 135 contacts and 134 are quarantined. The strain is Bundibugyo, which has no approved vaccine or treatment. The count keeps changing, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Outbreak response is a live case in duty of care, contact tracing and crisis communication that HR and brand teams are judged on.

items.title: US raises its Kenya travel advisory to Level 3
items.summary: Africanews reports that the United States raised its travel advisory for Kenya from Level 2 to Level 3 on 20 October, citing Ebola along with crime, kidnapping, terrorism, civil unrest and road safety. The advisory comes as Kenya's confirmed Ebola cases reached nine.
items.why: Travel advisories change corporate travel policy, insurance and where companies send people, which feeds HR planning for field roles.

items.title: Rubio holds talks with Jaishankar in Mumbai as India and the US try to finalise a trade deal
items.summary: AP, via KSAT, reports that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in Mumbai on 20 October. Rubio said the two sides are as close as they can be without having signed, with a few items left. The Week says energy, defence and West Asia are also on the agenda, and that he is expected to meet business leaders, then fly to Jamnagar on 21 October. A report on a possible waiver for India's Russian energy purchases is still under discussion, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: A US-India trade deal affects tariffs on Indian exports, which shapes hiring in export, retail and consumer firms that recruit MBAs.

items.title: Jio Platforms raises about Rs 8,110 crore from anchor investors; IPO opens today
items.summary: Business Standard, ThePrint and the Groww digest report that Jio Platforms allotted shares worth about Rs 8,109.9 crore to 212 anchor investors at the top of the Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 price band. Institutional bids exceeded Rs 2.5 lakh crore, about 30 times the anchor quota. The public issue opens on 21 October and closes on 23 October. Sources differ slightly on the exact anchor and issue size, so treat the figures as approximate.
items.why: A very large listing shows investor appetite for Indian consumer and telecom brands, and shapes how marketers think about brand value and employer branding.

items.title: Indian equity markets reopen today after the Dussehra holiday
items.summary: Newstrack and the Groww digest report that the exchanges were closed on 20 October for Dussehra and that normal trading resumes on 21 October. The Nifty last closed at 22,888.95 on 19 October, down 1.11%.
items.why: Market sentiment after a holiday sets the tone for recruiter conversations in finance and consulting.

items.title: Muhurat trading date is reported as 8 November, but not confirmed
items.summary: A Groww digest says the special Muhurat session will run from 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm on 8 November. A Newstrack report says exchanges have not yet announced this year's timings, so the date is unconfirmed until NSE or BSE issue a circular.
items.why: Diwali-season trading traditions are a common talking point in finance interviews.

items.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its in-house inference engine
items.summary: Tech Insider reports that DeepSeek released its in-house inference framework, DeepInfer, under an Apache 2.0 licence on 20 October. The report comes from a secondary outlet, so details of speed and cost claims are unverified.
items.why: Cheaper open inference lowers the cost of building AI tools, which matters for how marketing and HR teams will adopt them.

items.title: Anthropic launches a free open-source vulnerability scanner
items.summary: The Neuron's daily AI digest for 20 October says Anthropic released OSS Scanner, which runs free periodic vulnerability scans on critical open-source projects and can include a proof of concept and, where possible, a proposed patch. This comes from a newsletter summary, so check Anthropic's own announcement for details.
items.why: Security and trust in the software supply chain affects every company that buys HR and marketing software.

items.title: Amazon opens TorchNeuron in public beta, a day after Google's TorchTPU
items.summary: The same Neuron digest says Amazon released TorchNeuron in public beta so PyTorch workloads can run on its Trainium chips, one day after Google released TorchTPU. Treat details as secondary-source reports.
items.why: Competition among chip platforms is what brings AI costs down for ordinary businesses.
